segments.text: You scored eighty in Maths, and seventy in Science.

segments.text: Which is the better result?

segments.text: Maths looks better, right? Actually, it's Science!

segments.text: To see why, you need a z-score.
segments.caption: To see why, you need a z-score.

segments.text: A z-score tells you how far a value is from the mean.
segments.caption: A z-score tells you how far a value is from the mean.

segments.text: Not in marks, but in standard deviations.
segments.caption: Not in marks, but in standard deviations.

segments.text: The formula is simple.
segments.caption: The formula is simple.

segments.text: Take the value, and subtract the mean.
segments.caption: Take the value, and subtract the mean.

segments.text: Then divide by the standard deviation.
segments.caption: Then divide by the standard deviation.

segments.text: In Maths, the class mean was seventy-five, and the standard deviation was ten.
segments.caption: In Maths, the class mean was 75, and the standard deviation was 10.

segments.text: Eighty minus seventy-five is five.
segments.caption: 80 minus 75 is 5.

segments.text: Divided by ten, that's zero point five.
segments.caption: Divided by 10, that's 0.5.

segments.text: Just half a standard deviation above the mean.
segments.caption: Just half a standard deviation above the mean.

segments.text: In Science, the mean was sixty, and the standard deviation was five.
segments.caption: In Science, the mean was 60, and the standard deviation was 5.

segments.text: Seventy minus sixty is ten.
segments.caption: 70 minus 60 is 10.

segments.text: Divided by five, that's two!
segments.caption: Divided by 5, that's 2!

segments.text: Two whole standard deviations above the mean.
segments.caption: Two whole standard deviations above the mean.

segments.text: Compared fairly, Science is the stronger result.
segments.caption: Compared fairly, Science is the stronger result.

segments.text: The sign tells you the side.
segments.caption: The sign tells you the side.

segments.text: Positive is above the mean. Negative is below.
segments.caption: Positive is above the mean. Negative is below.

segments.text: Zero is exactly average.
segments.caption: Zero is exactly average.

segments.text: And the bigger the size, the more unusual the value.
segments.caption: And the bigger the size, the more unusual the value.

segments.text: For normal data, about ninety-five percent of z-scores fall between minus two and two.
segments.caption: For normal data, about 95% of z-scores fall between -2 and 2.

segments.text: Beyond three, either way, is a common outlier flag.
segments.caption: Beyond 3, either way, is a common outlier flag.

segments.text: And in machine learning, features like age and salary are turned into z-scores, so they share one scale.

segments.text: Here's the complete picture.

segments.text: A z-score is the distance from the mean, in standard deviations.
segments.caption: A z-score is the distance from the mean, in standard deviations.

segments.text: The sign shows the side. The size shows how unusual.
